rites.name: Osusamnaala
rites.text: Osusamnaala is the concept of resonance held within the Singing, the sounding in which the first roots of Oseivsizith condense from undifferentiated vibration. It is less a being than a tuning that gives the nascent world its first lasting shape.

rites.name: Khouthok
rites.text: Khouthok is the concept of resonance that threads the first roots of Oseivsizith as they condense out of the Singing. It is spoken of as the pattern by which groves learn to hold their shape and growing kingdoms learn to answer one another.

rites.name: Grokuzhak
rites.text: Grokuzhak is a concept of the Oseivsizith cosmos, a rule of weight that the Courts of the First Age set upon every trial that bound the worlds together. In the councils of the Courts it was spoken as the measure by which a door between two worlds could be judged sound or cracked.

rites.name: Vesiatheth
rites.text: Vesiatheth is the concept of a binding that holds a doorway open between two worlds, a principle the Courts recognised as the weight of a promise kept. In the Age of Sundering it was the thread that the councils tried, and failed, to keep whole when landfall split the old bonds apart.

rites.name: Veolastanum
rites.text: Veolastanum is the concept of a binding oath that was first spoken among the broken worlds of Oseivsizith during the Fall. It held that no shard of a sundered world would be claimed by force, and its principle is said to have steadied the sky when landfall first broke the old bonds between the stars.

rites.name: Meles
rites.text: A method where pilots improvise their own visual scouting routes when instruments fail or cannot tell debris from threats. It lets crews search for lost wreckage, survivors, and other goals when sensors are unreliable.

rites.name: Valeontium
rites.text: A hostile code sent into machine minds to corrupt their workings, causing crippled systems that leave a vessel exposed to enemy strikes.

rites.name: Corauseolus
rites.text: A vessel leaps between distant points without a plotted course, guided by a scatter of random numbers. The jump is a desperate gamble, risking being lost forever or striking something unseen.

rites.name: Veornus
rites.text: A practiced skill of noticing which disguised machine-folk hide among the crowd. Those who master it avoid being fooled, and a single failure can cost them dearly.

rites.name: Telium
rites.text: A pair of intimate techniques practiced by a skilled lover, referenced briefly after a private encounter. Later, a rival uses the knowledge of such a technique to provoke jealousy in a former partner.

rites.name: Cinia Nasor
rites.text: A mind-based gift that certain folk can wield, though few of the common population bother to learn it. Its workings are known to the people, yet it rarely sees everyday use.

rites.name: Tellanum
rites.text: A chant recited by synthetic beings who fear their final ending is near. They gather in fellowship, pleading for strength, understanding, and a measure of peace in the face of loss.

rites.name: Riarnistia
rites.text: A melody that a caretaking machine hums while testing a servant unit's limbs. During the check, the machine dances to it alongside a companion figure.

rites.name: Syazora
rites.text: Syazora is a mind-transfer lattice threaded through the cradles of Oseivsizith's stellar forges, letting a sentient construct's awareness be rewritten into a freshly grown shell the instant its old body fails. Its effect is near-endless continuity wherever the cradles stand, though its own memory decays with each transfer.

rites.name: Corenallia
rites.text: A practice that slows a living body's processes to a near halt so it can be carried across vast voyages or held in check against sickness. Those who master it can stall an unknown affliction in a patient.

rites.name: Coronor
rites.text: A banned class of armament that bends the flow of time itself. Its uncontrolled effects are feared so widely that the peoples of the stars forbid its making, though a desperate captain once fires one anyway.

rites.name: Telorausium
rites.text: A mind-born art lets a being weave a vivid illusion of surroundings around itself, and can invite others to walk within the same false world.

rites.name: Ryillora
rites.text: Ryillora is a concept that threads through the Three Futures of Oseivsizith, where each ending branches and the Library shelves them all. In the Age of the first sovereign, it is named as the principle that lets groves and growing kingdoms choose which future to stand in.
